bug_report:
H edit descriptor should flag as error with -std-f95 (or higher)
When an H edit descriptor is used in a format, only a warning is given when -std=f95 (or higher) is specified.  It should be an error, as are other ancient features that were deleted in F95 such as PAUSE and ASSIGN/assigned GO TO.

Note in the following example that PAUSE gives an error, whereas use of the H edit descriptor is only a warning:

wws@w6ws-4:/tmp/wws$ cat fmt1.f90
program fmt1
  implicit none

  pause 13

  print 100
100 format (1H ,"Hello World")
end program
wws@w6ws-4:/tmp/wws$ gfortran -std=f95 fmt1.f90
fmt1.f90:4:10:

    4 |   pause 13
      |          1
Error: Deleted feature: PAUSE statement at (1)
fmt1.f90:7:17:

    7 | 100 format (1H ,"Hello World")
      |                 1
Warning: The H format specifier at (1) is a Fortran 95 deleted feature
wws@w6ws-4:/tmp/wws$ 
wws@w6ws-4:/tmp/wws$ gfortran --version
